messages.subject: Where to define "predicted"
parts:
Stan and I are, like, buddies.  Well, a few squabbles (first it was ~ and +=, then <- and =, and now | is not or ... really?  On top of reals cannot become integers?) but we work things out.  Worth pointing out is this important sentence regarding variable scope in Stan the Man 2.12.0, section 29.2, page 320: "to make a variable accessible in the model and generated quantities block, it must be declared as a transformed parameter."
    In Stan's model block, I defined and assigned a variable called "predicted," so that Stan could calculate the log likelihood of observed given predicted.  To calculate PSIS-LOO or WAIC (post Stan), I need to use "predicted" again to calculate the log likelihood for each observed, again, but this time in Stan's generated quantities block so that he can save the point-by-point log-likelihoods for each sample.   If the variable "predicted" is defined in Stan's model block, Stan will insist he cannot see it in his generated quantities block.  He's like that sometimes.   If I try to define "predicted" in Stan's transformed data block, thinking, "Obviously predicted data goes with observed data," then Stan tells me that it is illegal to redefine data in the model block, "attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=transformed data", transformed data is data, OK?  Fine, be like that.  
    Upon resorting to RTFM, our squabble seems to be resolved.  I happily move the definition of "predicted" to Stan's transformed parameters block, ...  Stan looks at his model block and says "attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=transformed parameter." 
    I have nowhere left to define "predicted."  Stan is telling me that I cannot make a prediction in Stan's model block and re-use that prediction in Stan's generated quantities block.  My prediction is from a user-defined function of the data that is slow (advection, diffusion, and mortality of a time-series salmon smolts between dams on the Columbia River, see attached).  I cannot pull the log-likelihood calculation into my user-defined function because Stan will not be able to see "target += normal_lpdf(observed | predicted, sigma)" inside there.  I think I have to re-run my user-defined function to generate "predicted_again" in Stan's generated quantities block.  But Stan is cooler than that, right?  What am I missing?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Where to define "predicted"
parts:
> On Nov 19, 2016, at 3:59 AM, Scott Akenhead <sc...@s4s.com> wrote:
>
> Stan and I are, like, buddies. Well, a few squabbles (first it was ~ and +=, then <- and =, and now | is not or ... really? On top of reals cannot become integers?) but we work things out.

We don't anticipate more changes in the basic syntax other than
adding new operations and data types.

When we move to Stan 3, we'll take everything deprecated now and
remove it.

| is not overloaded in Stan, because Stan doesn't have bitwise OR.
Stan uses || for disjunction, like many programming languages.

> Worth pointing out is this important sentence regarding variable scope in Stan the Man 2.12.0, section 29.2, page 320: "to make a variable accessible in the model and generated quantities block, it must be declared as a transformed parameter."

This follows from the general principle that block variables are
only visible in their own block and later blocks and that
variables are only assignable in their own blocks. The model
block doesn't have any block variables, only local variables.

We've been debating whether to loosen this requirement, perhaps
removing transformed parameters altogether and just having the
model block have block variables. But then we're also thinking
of allowing Jacobians to be defined and incremented in the transformed
parameter block (so you could write a model that could be used
for both MLE and for MCMC).

We could also take variables declared at the top of the model block
and just treat them like transformed parameters. Unlike Perl,
I don't like having multiple ways to do the same thing syntatically.

Stay tuned for what we decide---it's an ongoing discussion, and as
with all of our discussions, we're happy to get feedback.

> In Stan's model block, I defined and assigned a variable called "predicted," so that Stan could calculate the log likelihood of observed given predicted. To calculate PSIS-LOO or WAIC (post Stan), I need to use "predicted" again to calculate the log likelihood for each observed, again, but this time in Stan's generated quantities block so that he can save the point-by-point log-likelihoods for each sample. If the variable "predicted" is defined in Stan's model block, Stan will insist he cannot see it in his generated quantities block. He's like that sometimes. If I try to define "predicted" in Stan's transformed data block, thinking, "Obviously predicted data goes with observed data," then Stan tells me that it is illegal to redefine data in the model block, "attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=transformed data", transformed data is data, OK? Fine, be like that.

> Upon resorting to RTFM, our squabble seems to be resolved. I happily move the definition of "predicted" to Stan's transformed parameters block, ... Stan looks at his model block and says "attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=transformed parameter."

You have to define it in the transformed parameters block.
Again, see the general rule above.

> I have nowhere left to define "predicted." Stan is telling me that I cannot make a prediction in Stan's model block and re-use that prediction in Stan's generated quantities block. My prediction is from a user-defined function of the data that is slow (advection, diffusion, and mortality of a time-series salmon smolts between dams on the Columbia River, see attached). I cannot pull the log-likelihood calculation into my user-defined function because Stan will not be able to see "target += normal_lpdf(observed | predicted, sigma)" inside there. I think I have to re-run my user-defined function to generate "predicted_again" in Stan's generated quantities block. But Stan is cooler than that, right? What am I missing?

Stan's not very particular about types and scope (see above).
Blame me---I'm the one that imposed strict scoping and typing
in the first place.

So you either have to define a variable in the transformed
parameters block and use it in the model block, or define
it as a local variable in the model block and then redefine
it in the generated quantities block.

- Bob

P.S. I saw a lot of that salmon and dam stuff at the fisheries meeting for
ADMB before the last quant ecology conference in Seattle. They're
nifty models.
